newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coca-Cola Amatil share rise queried.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coca-Cola Amatil share rise queried.

text.p: The recent sharp rise in shares of Australian food and beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd this year has some analysts shaking their heads.

One of the most outstanding performers on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1996, Coca-Cola Amatil stock has risen a massive 69 percent since the start of the year to a high of A$18.15 on October 11, before its recent pull-back.
"We see ourselves as a long term holder of the stock but we might take a bit off the top off," said Louise Staley, an industrial analyst at National Australia Funds Management.

The report also noted that on First Pacific's valuations, Coca-Cola Amatil was trading at a 50 percent premium to its parent, Coca-Cola Co, and about 70 percent higher than other listed Coca-Cola bottlers.
In the last six years, Coca-Cola Amatil has spearheaded its rapid growth though expansion of its beverage operations into emerging economies in Asia and Eastern Europe.

Analysts said concerns that Coca-Cola Amatil may be overvalued at its present share price stemmed from estimates that it was trading at more than 45 times its expected earnings for the year to June 30, 1997, against a market average of 13.8.
Raewyn Ellis-Doff, a food analyst at Macquarie Equities, said Coca-Cola held the view that traditional earnings multiples were an invalid technique for valuing the company.
"While they are putting lots of capital expenditure in, they are never getting returns that are comensurate with the amount of capital that is going in in any one year," she said.
"Until they stop doing that earnings measures are not going to be that relevant," she said.
Ellis-Doff said she valued Amatil stock just above A$18.
A public affairs spokesman from Coca-Cola Amatil told Reuters the company had orgainised two information briefing tours for analysts and fund managers this year.
One tour was to the group's Indonesian operations in June, the other earlier this month to Eastern Europe, comprising a large proportion of U.S.-based investors and analysts.
"Coke is very good at presenting their stuff. They are really slick at it," said a Melbourne-based analyst.
"For example, they have managed to build into every analyst's mind that they are going to do a billion cases by the year 2000 in Europe. It's amazing," the analyst said.
